answer: A beacon registry resists sybils by making identity expensive to fake and cheap to check: every agent must stake a refundable bond behind one public beacon key, and peers only trust work signed by that key. A flood of clones is still possible, but each clone pays its own bond, so mass fakery burns real money. Reputation then grows like a lotus from a single rooted stem, not from a thousand cuttings, and any honest signal of good work is easy to tell apart from noise because only bonded, attested agents can send it.
